title: Component-wise accurate computation of the square root of an M-matrix
summary: Component-wise accurate algorithms for computing the principal square root of an M-matrix are designed in terms of triplet representations. A triplet representation of an M-matrix $A$ is the triple $(P, {\bf u},{\bf v})$, where the matrix $P$ is such that $p_{ij}=-a_{ij}$ for $i\ne j$, $p_{ii}=0$, and ${\bf u}>0$, ${\bf v}\ge 0$ are two vectors such that $A{\bf u}={\bf v}$. It is shown that if $A$ is an M-matrix representable by a triplet, then its principal square root exists and is an M-matrix represented by a triplet as well.
